text.name: TextDesc2
text.text: The Philips CD-i was released in 1991 as a multimedia platform designed around CD-ROM technology. It was developed primarily as an interactive media device rather than a traditional game console, supporting educational software, video, music, and games. The system received several licensed Nintendo titles including Hotel Mario and the Zelda CD-i games. Other releases included multimedia applications, movies, and educational programs. The CD-i was one of the early attempts to combine home entertainment and interactive media using optical discs.
